---
title: "2. DC operating point"
subtitle: "Solve node voltages, branch currents, and power"
julia:
  env: ["JULIA_PROJECT=../../.."]
---

```{julia}
#| include: false
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("../..")
using Amber
```

An operating point is the circuit's steady DC solution. Capacitor currents are
zero and inductor voltages are zero; nonlinear devices, when present, are
solved at their bias point.

```{julia}
@circuit BiasedDivider(; supply=5V, top=2kΩ, bottom=1kΩ) begin
    gnd = ground()
    input = node()
    output = node()
    Source = voltage_source(input, gnd; dc=supply)
    Rtop = resistor(input, output; value=top)
    Rbottom = resistor(output, gnd; value=bottom)
    observe(voltage(output), current(Rtop), power(Rbottom))
end

circuit = BiasedDivider();
result = operating_point(circuit);
```

## Read values by name

Result accessors return vectors because the same interface also serves analyses
with many time or frequency points. An operating point has one point.

```{julia}
vin = only(voltage(result, :input))
vout = only(voltage(result, :output))
itop = only(current(result, :Rtop))
pbottom = only(power(result, :Rbottom))

(; vin, vout, itop, pbottom)
```

Use ordinary Julia to check the answer against hand analysis:

```{julia}
expected_voltage = 5V * 1kΩ / (2kΩ + 1kΩ)
expected_current = 5V / (2kΩ + 1kΩ)

@assert isapprox(vout, expected_voltage)
@assert isapprox(itop, expected_current)
```

## Inspect convergence

Analysis metadata lives in `result.stats`. Do not silently assume a nonlinear
solve succeeded:

```{julia}
result.stats[:converged]
result.stats[:iterations]
println(explain_failure(result))
```

`result_table(result)` converts the saved point and root node voltages to plain
named tuples, useful at boundaries to tabular tooling.

```{julia}
result_table(result)
```

::: {.callout-important}
Run the operating point before interpreting a nonlinear circuit. Small-signal
and noise analyses linearize around this bias condition, so a physically wrong
bias produces a mathematically valid but irrelevant answer.
:::
